introduction_markdown: General Certificate of Education (GCE) Board, Ordinary Level, June 2026. Additional Mathematics, Paper 2 (code 0575). Time allowed: two and a half hours. Answer ALL questions in SECTION A (Pure Mathematics, compulsory to all candidates) and ANY TWO questions from EITHER SECTION B (Mechanics) or SECTION C (Statistics and Probability). In Sections B and C, all questions carry equal marks. Candidates are expected to answer a combination of Section A and Section B OR Section A and Section C, but NOT a combination of all three. If Section B is chosen, Section C may not be chosen, and the other way round. All necessary working must be shown. No marks will be awarded for answers without brief statements showing how the answers have been obtained. Electronic calculators and Formulae Booklets are allowed. Where necessary take g as 10 m s^-2.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(i) Given that a circular cylinder of height $h$ and radius $x$, open at one end, has volume $27\pi\ \text{cm}^3$. Show that

(a) $h=\dfrac{27}{x^2}$. *[1 mark]*

[Volume of a cylinder $V=\pi x^2h$ and surface area of a cylinder open at one end $A=\pi x^2+2\pi xh$.]
questions.corrige_markdown:
The volume is $V=\pi x^2h=27\pi$. Divide both sides by $\pi x^2$:

$$h=\frac{27\pi}{\pi x^2}=\frac{27}{x^2}.\ \blacksquare$$

questions.enonce_markdown: (i)(b) Show that the surface area is $A=\pi x^2+\dfrac{54\pi}{x}$. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The surface area of a cylinder open at one end is $A=\pi x^2+2\pi xh$ (the circular base plus the curved surface). Substitute $h=\dfrac{27}{x^2}$:

$$A=\pi x^2+2\pi x\cdot\frac{27}{x^2}=\pi x^2+\frac{54\pi}{x}.\ \blacksquare$$

questions.enonce_markdown: (i)(c) Find the value of $x$ for which the surface area is minimum. *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Write $A=\pi x^2+54\pi x^{-1}$ and differentiate with respect to $x$:

$$\frac{dA}{dx}=2\pi x-\frac{54\pi}{x^2}.$$

At a stationary point $\dfrac{dA}{dx}=0$:

$$2\pi x=\frac{54\pi}{x^2}\ \Rightarrow\ x^3=27\ \Rightarrow\ x=3.$$

**Nature.** $\dfrac{d^2A}{dx^2}=2\pi+\dfrac{108\pi}{x^3}$. At $x=3$ this is $2\pi+4\pi=6\pi>0$, so the stationary point is a **minimum**.

(The minimum surface area is $A=9\pi+18\pi=27\pi\approx84.8\ \text{cm}^2$, with $h=\frac{27}{9}=3$ cm.)

**$x=3$ cm.**

Integrate term by term, using $\int x^n\,dx=\dfrac{x^{n+1}}{n+1}$ and $\int\cos x\,dx=\sin x$:

$$\int(3x^2+\cos x)\,dx=3\cdot\frac{x^3}{3}+\sin x+C=x^3+\sin x+C.$$

(Check by differentiating: $\frac{d}{dx}(x^3+\sin x)=3x^2+\cos x$ ✓.)

**$x^3+\sin x+C$.**
